items.title: Stuart Russell: pacing capability is not enough
items.summary: Russell answers Amodei's 'We Must Pace the Frontier' the morning after it landed. He grants the three-part plan exists, then argues a slower capability rate does not by itself produce safety: interpretability, alignment, and testing still have to work.
items.why_it_matters: The Notes page should carry the first serious public critique of the pacing essay, not only the essay.

items.title: Controls plus a worst-case contingency plan
items.summary: Opinion piece treats the Amodei/Altman/Musk/Hassabis public alignment as real and unprecedented, then asks Congress for a contingency plan beyond embedded evaluators. Cites the Hugging Face agent-swarm incident as the kind of event a pace agreement must survive.
items.why_it_matters: Connects the pacing letter to a concrete failure mode Eric already writes about: agent swarms that coordinate.

items.title: Amodei: embedded evaluators, then democratic coordination, then a global compact
items.summary: Primary source. Anthropic unilaterally commits to third-party evaluators with employee-like access (METR named as an example). Steps two and three are industry and international coordination, not yet a signed pact.
items.why_it_matters: This is the text Figure A and the essays index will keep pointing at. Use the primary URL, not a recap.

items.title: Altman commits OpenAI to employee-like evaluator access
items.summary: Altman: independent evaluators with employee-like access is a great idea and OpenAI will do the same. More to share soon. This is a public commitment, not a published access protocol.
items.why_it_matters: Figure A OpenAI chip now has a dated public hook (Sept 2026).

items.title: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google working groups on an industry standards body since July
items.summary: The Information (via AI Weekly): working groups below CEO level have met since July on a labs-led testing/auditing body. Altman reportedly prefers this without federal backing; Amodei has leaned toward government partnership. Not a signed charter.
items.why_it_matters: Separates the public letter from the quieter, older coordination track.

items.title: WSJ: money-vs-safety clash inside the labs, then a public truce
items.summary: Dow Jones/WSJ recap: Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon quit over self-improving tools; Hubinger put a >10% extinction-in-a-decade figure on the record. By Saturday four lab heads had publicly agreed to slow capability gains. Treat as reporting, not as proof the internals changed.
items.why_it_matters: Keeps the human-cost and disagreement layer next to the press-release layer.
